current_disclosures.summary: Nvidia records a valuation allowance to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount believed more likely than not to be realized based on all available evidence. Deferred tax assets are recognized as income tax benefits during the period if realization becomes more-likely-than-not.

Benefits from tax positions are recognized only if more-likely-than-not sustained upon audit based on technical merits. Interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits are included as a component of income tax expense.

comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred tax asset valuation allowance policy
comparisons.peer_summary: A valuation allowance is recorded for deferred tax assets unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not; conversely, if realization is deemed more-likely-than-not, existing valuation allowances may be reversed, resulting in a credit to income tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD utilize the 'more-likely-than-not' threshold to assess the realizability of tax-related assets, but they apply it to different instruments. NVDA applies this threshold to the recognition of benefits from tax positions (unrecognized tax benefits), whereas AMD applies it to the recoverability of deferred tax assets and the maintenance or reversal of valuation allowances.

sentences.text: We recognize the benefit from a tax position only if it is more-likely-than-not that the position would be sustained upon audit based solely on the technical merits of the tax position.

Unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not (a probability level of more than 50%), we will record a charge to income tax expense in the form of a valuation allowance for the deferred tax assets that we estimate will not ultimately be recoverable or maintain the valuation allowance recorded in prior periods.

comparisons.peer_summary: Tax liabilities involve complexities across multiple jurisdictions; the company accrues liabilities for uncertain tax positions based on estimates of potential audit outcomes, with reversals recognized if liabilities prove unnecessary.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AVGO disclose policies for recognizing tax positions based on the 'more-likely-than-not' threshold and explicitly address the treatment of interest and penalties. NVDA states its policy is to include interest and penalties in income tax expense, while AVGO recognizes liabilities for anticipated audit issues based on estimates of whether additional taxes, interest, and penalties will be due.

sentences.text: Our policy is to include interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax expense.

We recognize potential liabilities for anticipated tax audit issues in the U.S. and other tax jurisdictions based on our estimate of whether, and the extent to which, additional taxes, interest, and penalties will be due.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance and effective tax rate change
comparisons.peer_summary: The effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets in 2024. This allowance was recognized in the third quarter of 2024 after determining it was more likely than not that the assets would not be recoverable, largely due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position resulting from asset impairment and restructuring charges.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and INTC both describe the use of the 'more-likely-than-not' standard for tax assessments, but with opposite operational outcomes in the reported period. NVDA discloses a general policy for recognizing tax position benefits if the position is likely to be sustained. In contrast, INTC details a specific 2024 event where it determined it was 'more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable,' leading to the establishment of a valuation allowance.

sentences.text: We recognize the benefit from a tax position only if it is more-likely-than-not that the position would be sustained upon audit based solely on the technical merits of the tax position.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Income taxes and deferred tax asset realizability
comparisons.peer_summary: Estimating income tax provisions and deferred tax assets requires significant judgment and depends on the ability to generate future taxable income in jurisdictions like Japan, the US, Malaysia, and Taiwan.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU reference the 'more-likely-than-not' standard in the context of income tax estimates and deferred tax asset realizability. NVDA cites this standard for recognizing benefits from specific tax positions, while MU cites it in the context of forecasting future taxable income required to realize net deferred tax assets.
